title: Machine-readable project records and executable verification
context: The owner participates in product decisions and validation rather than implementation, and requests no human-facing repository guides.
authority: The owner's repository documentation preference and implementation request.
consequences: Agents need a compact entry point into maintained machine records.
Required license notices remain part of the repository and distribution.
revisit_when: A concrete repeated workflow cannot be served effectively by the current records and checks.
history_note: Common record metadata was added when repository continuity was established; the earlier decision remains applicable.
basis: Project owner requests no human-facing repository documentation.
decision: Use executable checks, JSON decisions, a JSON contract manifest and generated JSON reports.
skills: Do not duplicate repository rules in a new skill before a repeatable workflow exists.
references: Consult relevant upstream documentation or reference implementations for a concrete need. Reuse or adapt useful components while keeping unrelated architecture out of the product; record primary sources for adopted dependencies.
completion: Linux protocol tests do not satisfy a native Windows build or clean-machine acceptance.
m0_scope: Empty desktop shell, executable wire schemas, generated types, worker handshake, local harness and CI definition.
